name: Miro Boards
description: Miro Boards is a resource-qualified name for Miro, whose collaborative online workspace organizes visual planning, workshops, diagrams, research, and project coordination on shared boards.
agentUseSummary: Do not create a separate Miro Boards connection or install. Select the canonical Miro provider, which owns the Relay-managed OAuth grant and bounded board and item workflows. Relay can inspect authorized boards and items, prepare exact changes locally, and create or update supported items under the selected Miro approval profile; board administration, deletion, broad ingestion, exports, and arbitrary API calls remain blocked.

blocked.label: Create a separate Miro Boards connection
blocked.description: Miro Boards and Miro identify the same provider account, team grant, boards, items, OAuth authority, and REST API; a second connection would duplicate identity and state.

blocked.label: Install duplicate Miro board tools
blocked.description: Relay mounts supported Miro board and item operations once through the canonical Miro provider rather than publishing parallel resource-qualified tools and policies.

blocked.label: Administer Miro boards or teams
blocked.description: Board creation, copying, deletion, sharing, membership, organization, project, team, and enterprise administration remain outside the canonical Miro V1 boundary.

blocked.label: Run separate Miro Boards actions
blocked.description: Supported board reads, item reads, local drafts, and approved item writes belong to the selected canonical Miro connection and its existing Safe or Dangerously skip permissions profile.

approvalProfiles.label: Use Miro
approvalProfiles.description: No separate Miro Boards action is enabled because this source name identifies the board resource surface of the already converged canonical Miro provider.

runtimeSupport.description: No duplicate Miro Boards tools are mounted. OpenClaw uses the canonical Miro provider for supported bounded board and item workflows.
No duplicate Miro Boards tools are mounted. Hermes uses the canonical Miro provider for supported bounded board and item workflows.

providerSetup.blocker: Miro Boards is a resource-qualified label for the boards inside Miro, not a separate provider identity, account, authorization, or resource system. Publishing another card, Miro OAuth grant, credential record, callback, installation, approval policy, audit identity, or runtime adapter would duplicate the canonical Miro provider. The canonical provider's production OAuth app, distribution review, credentials, and live validation remain separately blocked until completed through its existing setup plan.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep this alias slug non-installable and direct discovery, setup, connection, installation, and execution to the canonical Miro provider. Use only its exact bounded board and item tools under the selected Miro connection and approval profile. Revisit only if Miro publishes a separately authorized product named Miro Boards with distinct identity, resources, scopes, and lifecycle.

evidence.supports: Miro's official product page presents its online whiteboard as the shared visual workspace for brainstorming, planning, diagramming, meetings, workshops, and collaboration under the Miro product.
Miro's help center defines a Miro board as an online workspace inside Miro and explains that boards are created and saved within a Miro team or space.
Miro documents one OAuth 2.0 app installation and authorization-code grant for REST access, including boards:read and boards:write scope authority and rotating access and refresh tokens.
Miro REST v2 exposes boards through the canonical Miro API and boards:read authority rather than a separately authenticated Miro Boards service.
Miro REST v2 retrieves cursor-paginated typed items from one explicit board under boards:read, matching the canonical connector's bounded board-item surface.
Miro REST v2 creates a sticky note on one explicit board under boards:write, matching the canonical connector's approval-required item mutation rather than a separate provider.
